LinkedIn support for companies and founders

A marketing virtual assistant can keep LinkedIn content and conversations organised. We use approved company page access and prepare personal profile content for the account owner to review.

Page and profile upkeep

A marketing virtual assistant can review the company description, headline, featured links and banner against approved positioning. Prepare profile updates and use company page roles for changes in scope.

Publishing and thought leadership

Build a calendar around audience questions, events and launches. Draft founder posts, company updates, newsletters, articles and document carousels. Prepare images, mentions and links before scheduling approved posts.

Engagement and inbox handoff

Your social media virtual assistant monitors agreed comments, mentions and page messages. Prepare replies using the brand’s guidance, flag sensitive questions and pass enquiries to the CRM owner.

Research and performance

Review relevant topics, hashtags, competitor activity and audience questions. Report impressions, engagement, clicks and follower changes with dates and post links, then suggest topics for the next review.

Writing, editing and ghostwriting

Organise creative assets, prepare branded graphics and flyers, edit approved clips, coordinate guest or crew schedules and prepare show notes, transcripts and publishing files.

Planning your support

Open the topics that matter to your team. These details explain how to prepare the work, review results and handle changes.

Take a campaign item from brief to release

A marketing team plans an email and a social post from one approved article. Both use an image that is still under review. The workflow needs to preserve the source copy, make the different versions easy to review and prevent either item from going live before the asset is cleared.

  1. 01

    Turn the request into an editorial item

    Give your marketing virtual assistant the audience, objective, source article, two output formats and final reviewer. Split the deliverables into separate tasks with one shared dependency for the image. A calendar date alone does not say what is ready to ship.

  2. 02

    Prepare previews in the correct channels

    Adapt the approved material to the agreed length and format. Attach previews and the current asset version to the review item. Flag any change to a claim or promise so the reviewer can distinguish it from routine formatting.

  3. 03

    Release the approved version

    Check the approval against the specific draft, link destinations and publication time zone. After scheduling or publishing, record the final link and update the calendar. Carry any unapproved derivative forward as a separate item.

When this support helps

Drafts are stuck in review.

Give each piece one reviewer, a due date and a place to record the decision.

Assets live in too many folders.

Create a source list and distinguish the approved versions from working files.

A newsletter is ready to send.

Verify the audience, links and preview. Record the approval before scheduling.

What we need from you

Brief template

Use fields for audience, format, objective, due date and approver. Show a completed example so your marketing virtual assistant can tell when source material or a decision is missing.

Asset library

Identify the folder or system that holds approved copy, images and templates. Before a campaign is scheduled, check the destination of every link and the version of each asset. Record what changed after review so the next item starts with current, approved wording, images and audience assumptions. Use version names that a reviewer can recognise without comparing several files by eye.

Publication rules

Confirm who can schedule or publish, which channels require preview links, and how to record approval. Agree when a time-sensitive exception should go to the campaign owner.

When a task needs your decision

An asset lacks permission to publish

Keep the item in review and note what evidence is missing. Offer an approved alternative only if the reviewer can confirm that it fits the brief.

Two reviewers send conflicting edits

Record both requests against the current draft and route them to the final approver. Do not schedule a version while the decision is open.

A date moves after scheduling

Check dependent items and time zones, update the calendar and ask the channel owner to confirm the new date before replacing the scheduled version.

Review the results

Approval trace

Pick a published item and follow it back to the approved draft, asset and reviewer. If any link is missing, improve how the handoff is recorded.

Release readiness

Look at the next week’s calendar and distinguish ready items from drafts waiting on an asset, review or decision. Assign someone to each blocked item.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you work with our existing brand guidelines?

Use a brand handoff with example copy, asset locations, approval owners and any claims that need review.

Who signs off before publication?

Name one reviewer and define how their approval is recorded before an item is scheduled.

Can you turn one approved piece into several formats?

Agree which versions are in scope, such as a newsletter excerpt or social post. Route changes in claims or tone back to the reviewer.

How are assets and versions tracked?

Use the agreed folder or project board to record the current draft, the approved assets and the final published link.

What happens when a brief is missing an asset or decision?

Flag the missing item, assign an owner and show which publication date it affects. Resume when the required material is approved.

Can you run paid ads or define our strategy?

Scope execution separately from strategy, ad spend and specialist production. Identify who owns budget and performance decisions.
